title: The deadline that wasn't
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Wood tells Chloe the deadline passed. Chloe tells him deadlines have phone numbers.

panels.composition: The dock at the boat launch. October dusk. CHLOE and WOOD at the end, feet over the water. Gully's uncle's shack behind, dark.

balloons.text: It's done. The deadline was the third.

image.prompt: two young people sitting at the end of a wooden dock at October dusk with their feet over the water, a dark shingle shack behind them, brush-pen black and white

balloons.text: I'm not calling Portland to beg a racket for a partial.
You'd be calling Portland to accept a yes.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man on a dock, stubborn, dusk light

panels.composition: Chloe, standing up. Looking down at him.

balloons.text: You're going to stay. You were always going to stay. I wrote it in your yearbook and I hated being right in advance.

image.prompt: a young woman standing on a dock looking down at a young man who stays seated

panels.composition: Chloe walking back up the dock. Wood at the end, not turning. The water. The strip's narrow panel again — the dock drawn longer than it is.

image.prompt: a young woman walking away up a long wooden dock at dusk while a young man stays seated at its end without turning, the dock drawn longer than it is, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Chloe cites the yearbook (#18). The strip cites itself for the first time.
